headline: Task force reviewed partner updates, overdose data, opioid abatement funds, and emerging drug trends; no formal votes were taken.
summary: Partners including United Way, NH National Guard, Nashua Prevention Coalition, Doorways, Merrimack PD, Greater Nashua Mental Health Center, and Harbor Care gave updates on programs, events, and services. The group reviewed AMR overdose data showing 10 overdoses and one fatality last month, heard an SSANA update on service increases and fatal overdoses, discussed housing and encampment issues, reviewed the Opioid Abatement Trust Fund balance of $446,528, and heard a presentation on unregulated intoxicants and emerging drug trends.

1 | P a g e  
 
City of Nashua 
Division of Public Health and Community Services 
 
Mayor’s Task Force on Substance Misuse Meeting 
 
Tuesday, 08/18/2026 
9:30 – 11 a.m. 
Facilitator: Bobbie Bagley, Director DPHCS        Location: City Hall Auditorium, 3rd Floor 
Minutes 
 Partner Updates  
United Way  
• United Way is conducting a two-month shoe drive. Flyers have been 
distributed throughout the community. Funds raised will establish a fund to 
assist individuals who need shoes. The goal is to collect 5,000 pairs of shoes. 
NH National Guard  
• The STASH trailer has been wrapped and is available for community events. 
This is a major project involving the National Guard.  
Nashua Prevention Coalition:  
• New Program Manager introduced: Iraida Munoz.  
• NPC will participate in the Back-to-School event and is collaborating with 
community partners. 
• Planning is underway for Red Ribbon Week in October, including activities with 
teens. Partners are needed. 
• The Lock It Up Campaign continues. Members were asked to share 
information about where lockboxes may be available. 
• The campaign is targeting schools through Bridges and developing an 
educational series in collaboration with community partners. 
Nashua Regional Planning Commission: 
• Funds are available to assist with treatment and recovery transportation. 
Flyers were distributed.  
Doorways: 
• Doorways is organizing a gathering and walk for individuals who have lost 
loved ones. The walk will take place Friday at 9:00 AM. 
Merrimack PD:  
• A Gas Station Drugs educational session will be held on August 26 at 10 
Prospect Street. A QR code is available for registration through the 
department's website. There are approximately 120 seats available. Members 
were encouraged to spread the word about the training. Teens may attend 
the Gas Station Drugs event with their parents. 
• Families can access educational information regarding what may be found in a 
teenager's bedroom. 
• Flex funds are available to support individuals with housing and substance use 
needs. Funds are currently available through September 30. 
• The state has provided additional Narcan boxes. Members who need a box
2 | P a g e  
 
were asked to send an email requesting one. 
Greater Nashua Mental Health Center:  
• Mental health services have moved to 3 Pine Street Extension. Walk-in 
services have restarted and have been very busy. There is currently no wait 
time for substance use disorder (SUD) services; individuals can be seen the 
same day. The Intensive Outpatient Program (IOP) is being visited by Public 
Health and Lamprey. 
Harbor Care:  
• Harbor Care has a couple of beds available at Cynthia Day Family Center. 
AMR Data 
• Slide presentation on AMR Data with information on opioid overdoses and 
opioid-related deaths.  
• During the data review, it was reported that there were 10 overdoses last 
month, including one fatality. This represents the lowest number of overdoses 
since data collection began, as well as the lowest number of fatalities, with 17 
reported. The report can be shared with members upon request, and 
members were asked to send an email if they would like a copy. The AMR 
report will also be distributed. The state recently released a report indicating 
that it is on track to record the lowest number of overdoses since reporting 
began.  
• An increase in reported Narcan use was also noted, and expired Narcan may 
still be provided for certain purposes. 
 
SSANA Update 
• SSANA reported a 56% increase within one year, with 334 individuals served 
and 154 unique individuals since last year. Two fatal overdoses were reported 
in July, bringing the total number of fatal overdoses this year to 14. 
Approximately 25% of contacts occur through street outreach. Safer smoking 
kits continue to be distributed, and Narcan distribution has increased. 
Although substance use has increased, street outreach efforts have also 
expanded. Trust issues remain a concern because some individuals have been 
arrested at SSANA, and vandalism has also been an issue. SSANA is currently 
looking for a new location. 
• Upcoming activities include Back-to-School events featuring food, Narcan, 
education, and community resources. Information was shared regarding the 
Rally for Recovery on September 19. Revive Recovery is planning a deep-sea 
fishing trip at the end of August, followed by a food event on September 26. 
Information was also shared regarding Camp Mariposa. The 10th Annual Golf 
Tournament will be held on October 10, and a ribbon-cutting event in 
Manchester is scheduled for October 16. Members were reminded to bring 
weights for the tents. 
Housing Services 
Update 
• Regarding housing and encampments, there were concerns of an encampment 
on E. Hollis Street. It appears Police Department responded and has since 
been cleared. Revive responded to a need for syringe cleanup and this has

been completed.  
• The warming station is scheduled to open on November 15,2026 at Elm Street 
Middle School, and staff hiring is expected to begin in September. 
Opioid Abatement 
Trust Fund and  
• The Opioid Abatement Trust Fund currently has received an additional 
$146,618 from the state treasury. The total in the fund is $446,528 
• Request for funding support is opening September 
• Annual Report for the Opioid Abatement Trust Commission is due in 
September 
• Discussion was also held regarding the Opioid Fatality Review Committee. It 
was discussed that another organization will have to facilitate the Committee. 
The group will meet next month to discuss this further. 
Slide Presentation 
on Unregulated 
Intoxicants and 
Emerging Drug 
Trends by 
Merrimack PD 
• The group discussed emerging drug trends and unregulated intoxicants 
currently appearing on the market in 2026.  
• There is concern that these substances are increasingly being targeted toward 
juveniles.  
• Legislation regarding unregulated intoxicants in neighboring states was 
discussed, along with New Hampshire's approach to regulation.  
• Further discussion is needed regarding laws surrounding the use and 
regulation of these substances.  
• The Board of Health was identified as a potential avenue for continued 
discussion and education, and it was suggested that education regarding these 
substances and their risks should also be brought to the college level. 
 
   
Next Meeting September 15, 2026
